hypotheses.construction_plan: Define a generic two-variable function T(θ_a, θ_b). The expression T(i,j) is obtained by specializing (θ_a, θ_b) to (i,j). The expression T(j,i) is obtained either by specializing (θ_a, θ_b) to (j,i) or by applying a permutation operator that swaps the arguments of the T(i,j) instance. Both instances share the same functional template T, differing only in argument order.
hypotheses.rationale: The two subexpressions are structurally related by a permutation of the two arguments of a common function T. This is a symmetry of the function-argument structure, and the sum T(i,j)+T(j,i) naturally arises as the symmetrized combination of the two permuted instances.
